name: Philip S. W. Goldson International Airport
before:
Belize's main airport, at Ladyville about 30 minutes drive from central Belize City, and fifth busiest in Central America.

It sits at an elevation of 5 metres. Both the airport and the whole of Belize City are at serious risk of flooding because of that low elevation and the coastal position, which is part of why the country moved its capital inland to Belmopan. The airport stayed where it is and remains the largest and busiest in Belize.

A new paved access road was completed in mid-2020, running from the George Price Highway across the Belize River directly to the terminal side of the airfield.

There is one runway on a 457 acre site.

The airport has a long military history because of the territorial dispute with Guatemala, and hosted British Forces Belize, including RAF Harriers. Price Barracks sits just north of the airport.

It is named after the politician Philip S. W. Goldson, who died in 2001.
after:
Belize's main airport sits at Ladyville, 10 miles (16 km) from downtown Belize City. The airport counted about 1.2 million passengers in 2024.

Its 457 acre site has one runway and lies just 5 metres above sea level.

It is named after the Belizean politician Philip Goldson.

claims.note: The operator calls it Belize's only international airport; Wikipedia (the archived copy the Overview was drafted from, source 1 throughout this ledger) says it remains the largest and busiest in the country. This also carries the old 'remains the largest and busiest in Belize', folded in here.

claims.claim: the operator's road advisory, check-in times and opening hours
claims.why: Held back: the operator's pages (read 23 September 2026) warn that roadwork and dredging are under way on the airport access road, so drivers should expect slower traffic and allow extra time; ask passengers to arrive 3 to 4 hours before departure; and give the airport's hours as 6am to 6pm daily, with services beyond that on request. The road warning is the most useful thing on the operator's site for an agent, but it is a notice that will date quickly and replaces nothing in the old text. For Andy to decide.

claims.claim: FCDO: taxis, arrival form, departure tax, hurricanes, airstrip security
claims.why: Held back: the FCDO says to take only registered taxis with green licence plates and agree the fare first; everyone passing through Philip Goldson International must complete an immigration and customs declaration form (the digital one is recommended before travel); the departure tax is usually in the airfare when leaving by air; the hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November; and after the hijacking of a domestic flight on 17 April 2025 the Belize Airports Authority tightened security at the municipal airstrips. Nothing in the old text to replace.

quote: Only take registered taxis with green licence plates. Always ask the fare before getting in, and expect to pay in cash.

the Belize Airports Authority has announced security enhancements across Belize’s municipal airstrips
All travellers transiting Belize through the Philip Goldson International Airport are required to complete an immigration and customs declaration form.
